title: Hemolysis Measurement of Plasma/Sample with Nanodrop ND1000
author: Hetty Helsmoortel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t3teqnn
materials: start ND-1000 software choose ‘Cell cultures’ change max. absorbance from 0.2 to 2 (rescales the vertical axis) change wavelength (lambda) to 414 nm

steps.title: Prepare workspace and aliquot plasma
steps.instruction: Go to room 120.042 on the 2nd floor (MRB1). Aliquot 3 µL of plasma into a separate tube; the tube may remain at room temperature.

steps.title: Clean sample pedestal
steps.instruction: Open the Nanodrop sample arm. Wipe the sample pedestal first with an ethanol‑dipped, dust‑free swab (swabs are located next to the machine), then with a dry, dust‑free swab.

steps.title: Blank calibration with water
steps.instruction: Pipet 1 µL of water onto the cleaned pedestal using reverse pipetting (use an unused water tube to avoid bubbles). Gently close the sample arm and click “blank” to calibrate. If the resulting wave shows peaks, repeat the pipetting and re‑blank.

steps.title: Measure water reference
steps.instruction: Open the sample arm and clean the pedestal with a dust‑free swab. Pipet 1 µL of water onto the pedestal using reverse pipetting (use an unused water tube). Gently close the arm and click “measure” to record the water reference sample.

steps.title: Measure plasma samples
steps.instruction: For each plasma sample: open the sample arm, clean the pedestal with a dust‑free swab, pipet 1 µL of plasma onto the pedestal using reverse pipetting, gently close the arm, and click “measure”. After measuring, clean the pedestal and close the arm before proceeding to the next sample.

steps.title: Export measurement report
steps.instruction: Select “Reports” → “Export Report Table Only”. Save the Excel table (no wavelength plots) to a USB stick.
